palette.notes: From text: red-haired hero in a blue jacket on cooler, darker mountain scenes; hair colour is the dash signal; Badeline is a monochrome double. All 3 TikTok sheets were off-subject (cosplay, news), so frames could not confirm.

lighting: Not seen in frames. Per text: flat sprite lighting; mood from per-chapter background colour and glow effects rather than shading on the tiny hero.
silhouette: Per text: tiny hero that still reads: big hair blob, clear head/body split, backpack bump. Badeline uses the same silhouette in monochrome so the double reads instantly.

motion.timing: Not measured and no on-subject frames. Per reviews and design: snappy, very short anticipation, fast dashes, brief holds on landings.

texture: Per text: clean tiles, little dithering; particles (dust, snow, dash sparks) carry the texture and energy. Team chose pixel art because it shows gameplay information clearly.
camera: Single-screen rooms with cuts between screens; screen shake punctuates dashes and hits. Cutscenes use a simpler, separate portrait art style.
sound: Lena Raine's score; the music informed the look of some levels.

acting.enters: Arrives on a fresh screen from the edge, mid-move, so each room starts with energy.
acting.acts: Whole-body acting on a tiny sprite: squash on landing, hair colour showing state, dust puffs on each step and wall-slide; emotion goes to cutscene portraits.
acting.exits: Leaves through the screen edge and the room cuts; no lingering exit.
acting.depth: One play plane; the monochrome double appearing in that same plane is the staging trick, plus close-up portraits in cutscenes.

techniques: hair as a state signal: colour change tells if the dash is ready
landing squash: 1-2 flattened frames before standing
afterimage trail of the silhouette on a fast move
dust and spark particles on every ground or wall contact
monochrome palette swap for an evil twin
short screen shake on big impacts
feel: tiny saturated hero + trailing hair + squash on every landing + shake on impact = big personality in a few pixels
for_fred: Give Fred one readable state signal (fin colour or glow) instead of more animations, and squash him 1-2 frames whenever he lands or stops. A monochrome 'shadow Fred' that pops in, copies him and leaves is a cheap second character that can come back later in the reel.
